Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

The first astronauts on Mars will need the best possible map. This guide layers data from several NASA Mars missions into one view of a Marswalk at Jezero Crater: where to walk, what the conditions are, and what science is on the way.

Layered, integrated view
Terrain, slope, radiation and dust layers on one map, plus a global locator for context. Terrain comes from MOLA / HiRISE-class elevation data; load the real NASA HiRISE Jezero DTM in the NASA data tab.
Routes and destinations
Click to set START and TARGET. Direct, Safest and Science routes show distance, time, steepest slope, dose and an elevation profile. Slopes over 25° are treated as not walkable.
Current conditions
Live Mars local time (LMST at Jezero), current season (Ls), temperature, pressure, dust opacity and dust-storm scenarios, plus a solar particle event switch. Future sols can be simulated.
Safe and quick, with science
The Survival tab turns suit power, O₂ and water reserves into a go / no-go call. The Science tab and route stops cover delta, olivine and carbonate targets seen by CRISM and Mars 2020.

Honesty note: terrain is synthetic until a DEM is loaded. Weather, dust and radiation are simple models informed by MEDA, REMS and RAD context, and are labelled MODELED in the interface. They are not live NASA measurements.

Credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona (HiRISE), MOLA, CTX, CRISM, MEDA, REMS, RAD, THEMIS, GRS. Not flight software; not endorsed by NASA.

Global locator: feature centres are plotted at true lat/lon, outline shapes and sizes are schematic. Terrain is synthetic until a real DEM is loaded; the simulated crater is sized like real Jezero (~45 km across) but its shape is idealised. This is a planning/simulation interface, not flight-certified operational software. REAL DEM means the elevation raster came from the loaded file; it does not mean weather, radiation, or mineralogy layers are live NASA measurements. Those layers remain explicitly modeled/reference data unless separately connected to source observations.
